To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the Nusselt solution is unstable for film Reynolds number Re30, (b) the instability is intrinsic to the laminar film flow and is not caused by transverse vibrations of condensing surface, (c) the instability leads to wave effects that grow over the laminar-turbulent transition range of Re30, (d) the wave effects can be enhanced or dampened by choosing appropriate wall noise through suitable actuators, (e) the wave effects increase heat transfer rates

the steady Nusselt solution of film condensation of quiecent saturated vapor on vertical wall is nonlinearly stable up to Re60 and that the wave effects due to the sensitivity of the film flow to the ever-present transverse wall vibrations are important in the transition zone of the film flow.
the steady-state solution of the Nusselt film condensation problem on a vertical wall is stable up to Re60.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the stability and wave phenomena associated with film condensation.
the nonlinear stability of the classical Nusselt problem of film condensation and wave effects.
the nonlinear stability and wave effects of the classical Nusselt problem of film condensation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the film flow in the Nusselt condensation problem is inherently unstable, and that this instability is the cause of wave fluctuations and the transition from laminar flow to turbulent flow.
the Nusselt solution is stable and the film is laminar for Re 30, and unstable and turbulent for Re 60.

the present study has established the following: (i) The Nusselt solution, as well as the linear stability analysis results, are valid only for a limited range of Re30; (ii) The Nussel solution is stable for 0 < Re30; (iii) The Nussell solution is unstable for Re30, and the instability is characterized by a wave number, k, of 1.5; (iv) For Re30, the Nusselt solution becomes unstable

we have shown that the film condensation problem is much more complicated than what has been thought for a long time.
the classical Nusselt problem is nonlinearly stable for the range of film Reynolds number up to Re60.
the classical Nusselt problem is not a simple one.

film flow’s sensitivity (intrinsic and extrinsic) to transverse vibrations can be used to control heat transfer rates.
the film flow is very sensitive to ever present minuscule transversal vibrations of the condensation surface.

the classical Nusselt problem of condensation on a vertical wall is inherently unstable, and that wave effects, which were not accounted for in Nusselt’s analysis, play an important role in the condensation heat transfer process.
